subject: Refund held due to EU reverse-charge on credit note — usage export requested

From: Marta Kowalska <marta.kowalska@supernova.ai>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: accounts-payable@supernova.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Refund credit held — reverse-charge applied to credit note RC-2233

Hi Rachel,

We received the credit note RC-2233 (issued 2026-11-11) but our bank is holding the refund because the invoice shows an EU reverse-charge VAT line. Our AP team says refunds/credits should not be reverse-charged back to us — Supernova is VAT-registered in PL and we expected a gross credit. Can you:

- Confirm how the credit note was rendered (reverse-charge vs gross)?
- Share the ledger export showing token-level usage for Nov 1–11 tied to our org (tenant_id: SNVA-01)
- Attach the original PO and remittance (we included PO and remittance in this thread)

Attachments: PO-8342.pdf (purchase order), remittance_20261111.pdf (bank remittance)

Thanks,
Marta Kowalska
Head of Finance — Supernova AI
Marta.Kowalska@supernova.ai
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Fwd: Refund credit held — reverse-charge applied to credit note RC-2233

Looping you both in — Supernova's refund is being held by their bank because the credit note shows reverse-charge. Ben, can ops generate a tenant-anchored usage export for SNVA-01 (Nov 1–11) and confirm whether the credit note applied VAT in our system or if it was an accounting transcription error? Jordan, can you advise on precedent for EU refunds (PL) — should we issue a gross credit or supply a corrected credit note?

Quick asks:
- Ops: CSV with usage rows, token counts, model, timestamps, invoice mapping (attach to reply)
- Finance: Guidance on whether we can re-issue RC-2233 as a gross credit and impact on VAT reporting

I propose we offer a provisional credit while we investigate to unblock payment. Happy to discuss on a quick call.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Original message attached below.
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 12:18:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Refund credit held — reverse-charge applied to credit note RC-2233

Thanks — ran the export for tenant SNVA-01, window 2026-11-01 00:00 to 2026-11-11 23:59 (attached). Key findings:

- Total gross usage tokens: 4,280,912
- Credit applied on RC-2233 maps to invoice INV-23091 (net: 8 21,340.00). The credit note was generated from that invoice template and picks up the invoice VAT treatment flag (reverse-charge=true) because the billing entity was set to 'EU - Default (reverse-charge)'.
- I see no double-billing or duplicated request ids in the exported sample. Usage rows include request_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, timestamp, invoice_id.

Attachment: usage_export_20261113.csv (CSV stub)

If Finance confirms the VAT treatment was incorrect, we can re-issue the credit note as gross. I'll standby to regenerate credit once we have the go-ahead.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Billing Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marta Kowalska <marta.kowalska@supernova.ai>
Cc: accounts-payable@supernova.ai, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:45:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Refund credit held — reverse-charge applied to credit note RC-2233

Hi Marta 2 thanks for flagging this and for the PO/remittance.

Quick update and proposed resolution:

- Ops delivered an export (attached) showing the usage tied to SNVA-01 for Nov 111. The credit note RC-2233 was generated with the 'reverse-charge' VAT flag because the billing entity on file for Supernova's account is set to 'EU - reverse-charge'. This looks like an onboarding configuration mismatch.
- To unblock payment immediately, we're happy to reissue RC-2233 as a gross credit (same gross/net amounts) and provide an updated PDF credit note and a corrected invoice credit transaction. This will not change the economics  it will only change the VAT presentation so your bank can process the refund.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You confirm you'd like the gross credit reissue (reply will suffice).
2) We'll reissue credit note and send corrected PDF + updated ledger export (expected turnaround: 24 business hours).
3) Finance will log a corrective memo for our VAT filings for the quarter; we'll share any supporting doc we produce for your records.

If you want a call to sign off, Jordan and I are available tomorrow 09:0011:00 CET.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: usage_export_20261113.csv (re-sent), credit_note_RC-2233.pdf (original attached for reference)
